## Summary

The PDL default of the block-sparse decode chain flips ON for cc 10.7: `SPARSE_DECODE_PDL_DEFAULT_CCS = ((10, 7),)` (it was empty).  A
caller-list `QsaSpec` block declared with `use_pdl=None` (the default) over bf16 / f16 pools on a cc 10.7 part now launches its chain -- the
norm + RoPE pass, the separate cache write, the separate sigmoid gate, the block-sparse core and its split combine -- under programmatic
dependent launch, exactly what `use_pdl=True` has done since the switch landed: the same kernels, `out` / the gated O / the LSE / the pools
bitwise the plain chain, eagerly and under CUDA-graph capture.

What stays: the explicit knob pins either way (`use_pdl=False` is the plain chain on cc 10.7, `use_pdl=True` is served on every part); every
other part reads False until measured there; the routes that decline the switch keep declining with the same typed reason (the in-block
indexer's decode step -- `QsaSpec(index_source="indexer")` --, `thd=True` on a `QsaSpec` geometry, e4m3 pools, the quantized pipelines), and
AUTO never resolves True where the explicit True is refused.  `DecodeEnvelope.pdl_default` reads the new tuple: True for the served
caller-list form on cc 10.7, False under the indexer and on every other part; the per-step reading is
`decode.pdl_default and decode.route(s_q, batch).pdl_capable` on the dense form and `decode.pdl_default` itself under `sparse_core` (the
sparse core carries the sites at every served step width; the dense route table does not apply there -- the comments / docs that stated
the dense formula for both forms are corrected, from a review comment on this PR).  No kernel change.  No `Capabilities` field or `EngineSpec` changes (a
knob-domain change); the docs' knob row and block-sparse PDL paragraph, the tracker's sentence that stated the old default, the constant's
docstring and every comment / docstring that said "empty until measured" now spell the new default.

## Why: measured on every served route, bitwise, no cell slower

The switched block was measured against the plain one in one process on one exclusive cc 10.7 GPU of the 212-SM class at the locked SM clock
(2376 MHz): CUDA-graph replay medians of A/B/A x 3 rounds x 100 iterations with the slots shuffled per iteration, every arm in the same
process over its own pool holding the same oracle-written prefix bytes, the served block built twice per process as its own control twin (the
pair's magnitude, floored at 1 %, is the cell's band), every numerics oracle before timing (the PDL arm must be bitwise the plain arm), the SM
clock sampled during the timed rounds and the power-cap counters read before and after every process (no event).  Speed-ups are POSITIVE
`baseline / new - 1`; SOL % = the step's own HBM bytes under the whole-layer byte model against that GPU's measured HBM copy bandwidth, the HBM
term.  Under `"auto"` the body is the lean tile at B 1 (batch x KV heads <= 4 CTAs per chunk) and the tcgen05 core at B 4 and B 32, so both
bodies are covered on the route that serves them.

### Batch 1: the lean decode tile (the AUTO body there), the caller-list block, shared list

Baseline = the lean body as served (PDL off); FROST = the same body under `use_pdl=True` (bitwise the same output); the tcgen05 core (pinned explicitly) for context.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 8K x 1 | 35.4 | 34.9 | +1.3 % | 23.1 / 23.4 | yes | 37.3 | 35.4 / 34.9; +1.3 % | -1.46 % |

### Batch 4 and batch 32: the tcgen05 core (the AUTO body there), the caller-list block, shared list

Baseline = the block as served (the core, PDL off); FROST = the same block under `use_pdl=True` (bitwise the same output); the core pinned explicitly and the serving stack's own QSA layer for context.

Geomean of the PDL speed-up over the batch-4 / batch-32 rows of record: +2.6 % (the symmetric reading over the four pairs built in the other order: +2.3 %; every rotated PDL arm bitwise its plain twin, the rotated control pairs within +0.41 %); over the batch-1 rows +1.4 %.  The rule under which
the default may flip for a bitwise, performance-only launch attribute: a cell LOSES if PDL is slower than the plain block beyond that
process's control band; the default flips only if no measured cell loses, every PDL arm is bitwise its plain arm, every oracle passes and
the clock reads clean, with every served route covered.  Result: 13 of 13 cells pass, no cell slower, every PDL arm bitwise, every control
pair within its band -- so the default follows the measurement.  (The earlier per-step bar of >= 1.0 us and >= 5 % that kept the switch
explicit was written for a new kernel body; a launch attribute that changes no bit and loses nowhere is held to "never slower" instead.)

## The change

* `python/cudnn/gated_attention_block/api.py`: `SPARSE_DECODE_PDL_DEFAULT_CCS = ((10, 7),)`; its docstring states the domain (caller-list
  `QsaSpec` blocks over bf16 / f16 pools; never the in-block indexer, never `thd=True`), the switched stages and the measurement; the knob
  comment, the envelope's field comment and construction comment, `_pdl_default`'s and `serving_envelope`'s docstrings say the same.  The
  resolution code is untouched (`_pdl_default` already read the tuple).
* `docs/fe-oss-apis/gated_attention_block.md`: the `use_pdl` knob row (auto True on the block-sparse decode mode's caller-list block on cc
  10.7) and the block-sparse PDL paragraph (the measured table in words).
* `python/cudnn/sdpa/frost/SUPPORT_MATRIX_TRACKER.md`: the DECODE-form knobs paragraph's PDL sentence (it stated "kept empty"); no
  `Capabilities` row changes.
* Review follow-up (text only): the per-step PDL guidance in the envelope's field comment, `serving_envelope`'s docstring, the envelope
  construction comment and the docs' paragraph + knob row now says the dense formula applies to the dense form and `decode.pdl_default`
  itself under `sparse_core` (the dense route table reports `pdl_capable=False` past 32 rows while the sparse core takes the switch there).

## Tests (RED first)

The expectations were flipped first and run against the unchanged tuple, then the tuple flipped and the same tiers re-run (an A100 host
through the branch's own import; the Rubin cells skip there):

* `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_qsa_decode.py`: the AUTO-reading test (renamed
  `test_pdl_auto_resolves_true_on_the_sparse_form_on_the_measured_part_and_the_envelope_says_so`) reads AUTO True on cc 10.7 with the same
  switched stages as the explicit True, the explicit False the plain chain, False on cc 10.0 and under the tuple patched empty (the explicit
  True still served), and the envelope's `pdl_default` the same way (the dense form keeps its own tuple); the in-block indexer test now reads
  the SHIPPED tuple (no patch) and keeps the decline route: AUTO False, the explicit True refused by name, the envelope False with no switched
  stage under the indexer and True with the four stage kinds on the caller-list form.
* `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_serving_pdl.py`: the one-domain test reads the sparse block and the indexer-band
  block True under AUTO (the same stages as the explicit True), the explicit False off, the indexer's decode step still declined.
* RED (the tests flipped, the tuple unchanged): the block set (`test_block_qsa_decode.py` + `test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py` + `test_block_serving_pdl.py` + `test_block_serving_decode.py`) **3 failed / 93 passed / 285 skipped** -- exactly the three flipped tests (their first assertions: `assert () == ((10, 7),)` in the two AUTO-reading tests, `assert (10, 7) in ()` in the indexer test); the lean module (`test_sdpa_fwd_sparse_lean_sm107.py`) **46 passed / 88 skipped**; the wider sweep (`test_sdpa_fwd_heuristics.py` + `test_sdpa_fwd_sparse_sm107.py` + `test_block_qsa.py`) **397 passed / 202 skipped**.
* GREEN (the tuple flipped): the block set **96 passed / 285 skipped**, the lean module **46 passed / 88 skipped**, the wider sweep **397 passed / 202 skipped** -- the three flipped tests pass, nothing else moved.

## Validation (functional; the performance numbers are the measurement above)

* Development class (cc 10.7, 204 SMs, a shared GPU, functional only) on the pushed head with the extension built for its base: NOT RUN at the time of opening -- the shared development node was unreachable at the network level for the whole session; the four selections (the lean module's Rubin tier, the block decode module's lean-tile and PDL cells, the end-to-end module's decode steps, the tcgen05 core's own module; 101 / 22 / 1 / 347 passed on the previous change of this file set) are owed and will be posted as a comment once the node is back.  The CI lanes on cc 10.7 (`python/*/cutedsl` and `python/sdpa/frost`) run these modules with the default flipped.
  With the default flipped, every block decode cell that declares a caller-list block under AUTO runs the chain under PDL on the device,
  and the module's own PDL cells (bitwise vs the plain chain, the first-execute capture, the launch census) run alongside.
* `black -l 160` + the pre-commit hooks on the changed files; SPDX headers untouched.

## Not in this change

* FlashInfer: its entry declines the switch under the in-block indexer (the route it serves), so no re-vendor is needed for this change; a
  later re-vendor picks the new default up through this constant.
* The named-barrier lever on the sparse core (a kernel change, measured separately) and the k >= 2 cap of the lean tile (its sub-tiles per
  CTA stay 1).
* Every other part keeps the AUTO reading False until measured there; the in-block indexer's decode step and the packed (`thd=True`) form
  keep their typed declines.

detail.body:
## Summary

The PDL default of the block-sparse decode chain flips ON for cc 10.7: `SPARSE_DECODE_PDL_DEFAULT_CCS = ((10, 7),)` (it was empty).  A
caller-list `QsaSpec` block declared with `use_pdl=None` (the default) over bf16 / f16 pools on a cc 10.7 part now launches its chain -- the
norm + RoPE pass, the separate cache write, the separate sigmoid gate, the block-sparse core and its split combine -- under programmatic
dependent launch, exactly what `use_pdl=True` has done since the switch landed: the same kernels, `out` / the gated O / the LSE / the pools
bitwise the plain chain, eagerly and under CUDA-graph capture.

What stays: the explicit knob pins either way (`use_pdl=False` is the plain chain on cc 10.7, `use_pdl=True` is served on every part); every
other part reads False until measured there; the routes that decline the switch keep declining with the same typed reason (the in-block
indexer's decode step -- `QsaSpec(index_source="indexer")` --, `thd=True` on a `QsaSpec` geometry, e4m3 pools, the quantized pipelines), and
AUTO never resolves True where the explicit True is refused.  `DecodeEnvelope.pdl_default` reads the new tuple: True for the served
caller-list form on cc 10.7, False under the indexer and on every other part; the per-step reading is
`decode.pdl_default and decode.route(s_q, batch).pdl_capable` on the dense form and `decode.pdl_default` itself under `sparse_core` (the
sparse core carries the sites at every served step width; the dense route table does not apply there -- the comments / docs that stated
the dense formula for both forms are corrected, from a review comment on this PR).  No kernel change.  No `Capabilities` field or `EngineSpec` changes (a
knob-domain change); the docs' knob row and block-sparse PDL paragraph, the tracker's sentence that stated the old default, the constant's
docstring and every comment / docstring that said "empty until measured" now spell the new default.

## Why: measured on every served route, bitwise, no cell slower

The switched block was measured against the plain one in one process on one exclusive cc 10.7 GPU of the 212-SM class at the locked SM clock
(2376 MHz): CUDA-graph replay medians of A/B/A x 3 rounds x 100 iterations with the slots shuffled per iteration, every arm in the same
process over its own pool holding the same oracle-written prefix bytes, the served block built twice per process as its own control twin (the
pair's magnitude, floored at 1 %, is the cell's band), every numerics oracle before timing (the PDL arm must be bitwise the plain arm), the SM
clock sampled during the timed rounds and the power-cap counters read before and after every process (no event).  Speed-ups are POSITIVE
`baseline / new - 1`; SOL % = the step's own HBM bytes under the whole-layer byte model against that GPU's measured HBM copy bandwidth, the HBM
term.  Under `"auto"` the body is the lean tile at B 1 (batch x KV heads <= 4 CTAs per chunk) and the tcgen05 core at B 4 and B 32, so both
bodies are covered on the route that serves them.

Baseline = the block as served (the core, PDL off); FROST = the same block under `use_pdl=True` (bitwise the same output); the core pinned explicitly and the serving stack's own QSA layer for context.

process's control band; the default flips only if no measured cell loses, every PDL arm is bitwise its plain arm, every oracle passes and

pair within its band -- so the default follows the measurement.  (The earlier per-step bar of >= 1.0 us and >= 5 % that kept the switch
explicit was written for a new kernel body; a launch attribute that changes no bit and loses nowhere is held to "never slower" instead.)

## The change

* `python/cudnn/gated_attention_block/api.py`: `SPARSE_DECODE_PDL_DEFAULT_CCS = ((10, 7),)`; its docstring states the domain (caller-list

  construction comment and the docs' paragraph + knob row now says the dense formula applies to the dense form and `decode.pdl_default`
  itself under `sparse_core` (the dense route table reports `pdl_capable=False` past 32 rows while the sparse core takes the switch there).

The expectations were flipped first and run against the unchanged tuple, then the tuple flipped and the same tiers re-run (an A100 host
through the branch's own import; the Rubin cells skip there):

* `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_qsa_decode.py`: the AUTO-reading test (renamed
  `test_pdl_auto_resolves_true_on_the_sparse_form_on_the_measured_part_and_the_envelope_says_so`) reads AUTO True on cc 10.7 with the same
  switched stages as the explicit True, the explicit False the plain chain, False on cc 10.0 and under the tuple patched empty (the explicit
  True still served), and the envelope's `pdl_default` the same way (the dense form keeps its own tuple); the in-block indexer test now reads
  the SHIPPED tuple (no patch) and keeps the decline route: AUTO False, the explicit True refused by name, the envelope False with no switched
  stage under the indexer and True with the four stage kinds on the caller-list form.
* `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_serving_pdl.py`: the one-domain test reads the sparse block and the indexer-band
  block True under AUTO (the same stages as the explicit True), the explicit False off, the indexer's decode step still declined.
* RED (the tests flipped, the tuple unchanged): the block set (`test_block_qsa_decode.py` + `test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py` + `test_block_serving_pdl.py` + `test_block_serving_decode.py`) **3 failed / 93 passed / 285 skipped** -- exactly the three flipped tests (their first assertions: `assert () == ((10, 7),)` in the two AUTO-reading tests, `assert (10, 7) in ()` in the indexer test); the lean module (`test_sdpa_fwd_sparse_lean_sm107.py`) **46 passed / 88 skipped**; the wider sweep (`test_sdpa_fwd_heuristics.py` + `test_sdpa_fwd_sparse_sm107.py` + `test_block_qsa.py`) **397 passed / 202 skipped**.
* GREEN (the tuple flipped): the block set **96 passed / 285 skipped**, the lean module **46 passed / 88 skipped**, the wider sweep **397 passed / 202 skipped** -- the three flipped tests pass, nothing else moved.

* Development class (cc 10.7, 204 SMs, a shared GPU, functional only) on the pushed head with the extension built for its base: NOT RUN at the time of opening -- the shared development node was unreachable at the network level for the whole session; the four selections (the lean module's Rubin tier, the block decode module's lean-tile and PDL cells, the end-to-end module's decode steps, the tcgen05 core's own module; 101 / 22 / 1 / 347 passed on the previous change of this file set) are owed and will be posted as a comment once the node is back.
